analysis: The only change is in scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py (head lines 288-293). The test test_warming_cannot_publish_or_seed_default_branch_from_pr now pins the warm workflow's runs-on to a conditional expression: PR events use a routed runner (fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)['warm']) and everything else uses the literal blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27. It also pins a 'warm macos_arm64 blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27 ...' routing line in provider-release-cache.yml. This is a test-only assertion and ships no runtime code or provider/coordinator behavior, so none of the provider threat model's assets or trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, A-001, A-003) are affected. The security-relevant guards stay intact: no pull_request_target or workflow_run, no secrets., contents: write, aws s3 or notarytool in WARM/ACTION, and master/dispatch warming that feeds release builds stays on the literal Blacksmith runner. Untested unverified contract: the actual provider-release-cache.yml change (the route job, the Darkbloom Sandbox runner for PR warming, and cache isolation between PR sandbox runners and master-seeded caches) is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that PR-triggered warming on a sandbox runner cannot seed caches consumed by release builds (cache poisoning) and that the route job output is not attacker-controlled. This test does not weaken any check; it only adds stricter assertions.
